rationale: The assistant reached the right leading suspect ('the battery is the leading suspect') with appropriate hedging and a sensible handheld-vs-tools test, and did not give unsafe instructions. However it never asked for the model label ('V-something' was left unresolved), never asked about Max mode, never suggested checking charger pin contact, and never pointed the customer to Dyson support for a diagnosis before spending '£60+'. It also kept a floorhead restriction alive as a 'secondary possibility' despite blockages being ruled out and the handheld still cutting out, and the closing advice 'not to gamble on a battery blindly' gives no concrete way to avoid doing so.
